policy: Official links may be accepted within their checked identity, status, version, language, date and subject. Selected local TAR dataset texts are accepted only as dated source snapshots with attribution under the dataset CC BY 4.0 licence; they do not establish currentness. Prefer the government-published e-TAR consolidated edition for current-law questions. External-link acceptance, local-copy acceptance, topic coverage and country review completion are separate decisions.

publisher_assessment.decision: The Register of Legal Acts (e-TAR), maintained by the Seimas Chancellery, is accepted as Lithuania’s official legal publication and consolidated-text reference source within each record’s displayed edition and scope. Its registry pages expose legal-act identity, status, edition dates and chronology. The Lithuanian Open Data Portal TAR dataset is accepted only as a separate metadata/snapshot source, not as the dependable current-version selector.
publisher_assessment.basis: The official e-TAR FAQ states that registration/publication in the Register is official publication and directs users to select the currently valid consolidated edition; live official records show the Aliens Law edition 2026-07-01 to 2026-10-31, the Public Administration Law edition 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31, and other act-specific edition ranges. The official e-TAR edition list shows the Civil Code edition in force on 2026-10-21. The official portal gives stable record identifiers and edition histories.
publisher_assessment.limits: Primary legislation is in Lithuanian. The TAR dataset API exposes versioned text snapshots, but its open-ended status is not a dependable current-version selector; several records conflict with e-TAR editions and two card-procedure snapshots are repealed. Use the specific e-TAR consolidated edition for the relevant date. The external references do not establish legal-topic adequacy.
publisher_assessment.local_copy_and_reuse: Thirteen Lithuanian statutory texts are retained as dated, attributed snapshots from the TAR open-data dataset, whose portal record lists CC BY 4.0. The two HTML page conversions (N-Lex country information and the dataset description) remain link-only; they are not accepted local source texts. The dataset licence does not extend to unrelated e-TAR pages, guidance, forms, court decisions or mission content. No recurring mirror is proposed.
